verdict: Honeycomb is a clean, correctly tuned and well explained hold-and-respin, but under the apiary skin it is Money Respin on a ways board, and its full-comb climax hardly ever happens.
pros: Every measured band is met, and the feature carries 43% of RTP at 1 in 118 with an average of 49x: a solid, honest hold-and-respin.

The feature state is always readable: locked cells are framed with xN badges, the rest of the board dims, and Respins left / Bonus total / Comb n/25 stay on screen. The panel player understood every rule correctly.
The comb framing gives the grid fill a themed goal (Comb n/25, full comb 1,000x), and the art palette is coherent.
cons: The feature is a near-copy of Money Respin / Lightning Link. Add one theme-native rule that changes how respins play, for example a Queen bee landing in a respin that fills or doubles the adjacent cells, or capped cells that spread honey to a neighbour. That gives the slot something a player would describe to a friend.

The full comb is effectively unreachable (the 1,016x round reached 11/25). Make filling the comb pay its way: add tiered fill bonuses at 15/20/25 cells, or a meter that unlocks extra rows of the comb, so the theme's climax drives the payout instead of the x500 draw.

The worker bee wild reads as a mushroom with no WILD mark: draw it as a clear bee in flight with a 'WILD' ribbon, and give premiums a framed or deeper-coloured tile so they stand apart from the gold/cream lows.

The base game is silent about the chase: show each honey cell's value badge in the base game, add a 'Honey n/6' counter, and tease when 4-5 cells land (only while 6 can still complete). Round pays like 0.0046x up to readable steps so the paytable doesn't show four decimals.
confusions: The worker bee looks like a mushroom and has no WILD label; I only learned it was wild from the paytable.
Honey cells show no value in the base game, so before the paytable I couldn't tell if they paid or what they did.
There's no on-board counter of honey cells toward the 6 needed: a spin with 5 cells passed silently.
